decision: Dubbo becomes a ServerProvider plugin that supplies ToolMapping overrides, not a fork of the command/godzilla plugins
reason: The user asked for provide-style dependencies on the two upstream plugins; duplicating their providers would fork their tool configs and generators
evidence: Upstream AbstractServer#getToolMappingOverrides is merged into the registry tool mapping by MemShellRegistry; ProvidedPluginsTest asserts the upstream names and both Dubbo transports resolve

decision: Migrate proxy Dubbo support too, and carry its client tooling into dubbo-client
reason: The upstream proxy plugin advertised ProxyDubboService; deleting the upstream Dubbo server without moving the proxy template would leave a dangling mapping, and deleting tools/proxy would orphan its client
evidence: ProxyShellToolProvider mapping, ProxyDubboService, tools/proxy sources copied; DubboGenerationTest covers Proxy for both transports

decision: Fix upstream ByteBuddyShellGenerator to consult the server's injector template classloader
reason: The shell template lives in the plugin jar while the tool config class comes from the upstream tool jar; the old lookup could not see the plugin template
evidence: plugin-verification loads the real shadow jar through PluginBootstrap and generates every tool/transport; it failed before the fix and passes after it

decision: Ship the Dubbo signature stubs inside the plugin jar
reason: Upstream server-dubbo did the same; the generation engine reads template bytes and needs the referenced signatures resolvable at generation time
evidence: shadowJar contains com/alibaba/dubbo and org/apache/dubbo stub classes and excludes host and upstream tool classes

decision: Remove all Dubbo code paths from the upstream repo
reason: The user requires the upstream project to have nothing to do with Dubbo
evidence: Upstream server-dubbo, stub-dubbo, vul-dubbo, tools/command and tools/proxy removed; Dubbo constants, contracts, mappings, tests, CI job and docs removed

decision: Drop the Dubbo-specific ToolParamVisibility and result-label rules instead of moving them behind a new host SPI
reason: The rules are cosmetic UI hints; a new extension point would widen host API for one plugin, and the user asked for separation, not host redesign
evidence: Web and desktop fields now follow the generic WebSocket rule; plugin behavior is unaffected

decision: Apply group and version to all projects, not only the root
reason: The root assignment left every module at version "unspecified", so the shadow jar had no version and release metadata was wrong
evidence: ./gradlew :dubbo-plugin:properties reported version unspecified before the change; shadowJar now emits memshell-dubbo-plugin-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar

decision: Make CI verify the downloaded artifact, not only the freshly built one
reason: The user requires the CI artifact to download and work; a package job alone proves neither
evidence: verify-artifact downloads the uploaded artifact, runs sha256sum -c, then runs PluginBootstrap against that exact jar via -PdubboPluginJar with upstream host snapshots from Sonatype

decision: Gate packaging on both unit and integration jobs
reason: An artifact is only published from a commit whose unit and container suites passed
evidence: package needs [unit-test, integration-test]; integration runs the six provider scenarios on ubuntu-22.04 with Docker

decision: Quiet Testcontainers and Docker DEBUG logs in the integration tests instead of dropping the CI report step
reason: The tests passed but the junit-report action failed with Node's 0x1fffffe8 string limit because one container XML was 636 MB of Docker command dumps
evidence: Added integration-test/src/test/resources/logback-test.xml; the three container XMLs now total 692 KB and the report action gets a small input

decision: Add a second Dubbo transport that injects a virtual DubboExporter instead of exporting a ServiceConfig
reason: The request asked for the paper's Exporter memshell, which registers a control path in DubboProtocol's exporter map and exposes no service interface, so it works without a registry or helper interface
evidence: ApacheDubboExporterInjector and AlibabaDubboExporterInjector put a proxy Invoker under serviceKey(port, path, null, null); the injector parses raw $invoke because the exporter bypasses the filter chain; DubboGenerationTest asserts exporter types have no helper bytes and a control path derived from the shell class name

decision: Return AsyncRpcResult from the Apache exporter and RpcResult from the Alibaba exporter
reason: DubboProtocol.reply calls Result.thenApply; AppResponse throws there in 2.7.x and 3.x, while Alibaba 2.6 returns the Result directly
evidence: integration tests on 2.7.6/2.7.7/2.7.8/2.7.23/3.3.6 failed with 'AppResponse represents an concrete business response' before the wrapper; all five pass after

decision: Register the virtual control path with PermittedSerializationKeeper on Dubbo 3
reason: Dubbo 3 rejects decoding for any service absent from that keeper before the exporter map is consulted, so the injected exporter was unreachable from a 3.x client
evidence: provider log showed 'Service <path>:0.0.0 not found, invocation rejected' at DecodeableRpcInvocation.decode; ApacheDubboExporterInjector now registers a URL carrying the control path, and the 3.3.6 exporter tests pass

decision: Verify the Godzilla exporter with the real Godzilla wire protocol and a payload that executes a command
reason: Data transport through the shell is only proven when decrypted input reaches a live process; a marker payload would pass even if the payload stage never ran a command
evidence: GodzillaProtocol and GodzillaCommandPayload in dubbo-client; assertExporterGodzilla sends 'id' and expects a uid= line on all six scenarios

decision: Fold the Apache 2.7.x assertions into one parameterized test method per scenario
reason: Testcontainers 2.x stores shared containers as closeable resources in the enclosing test template's context store, so the store closes and calls stop() after the first parameterized method, leaving later methods without a container
evidence: The split-method version passed the first method's four scenarios and failed the rest with 'Mapped port can only be obtained after the container is started'; the merged method passes all four scenarios
